stem.en: Which of the following is a benzylic halide?

explanation.en: In C₆H₅CH₂Cl the halogen is on an sp³ carbon attached to the benzene ring: a benzylic halide. C₆H₅Cl is an aryl halide, CH₂=CHCl vinylic and CH₂=CHCH₂Cl allylic.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃CBr is:

explanation.en: The longest chain has three carbons; C-2 carries both Br and a methyl group: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (common name tert-butyl bromide).

stem.en: Which carbon–halogen bond is the longest?

explanation.en: Bond length grows with the size of the halogen: C–F 139 pm < C–Cl 178 pm < C–Br 193 pm < C–I 214 pm.

stem.en: Among CH₃F, CH₃Cl, CH₃Br and CH₃I, the largest dipole moment is shown by:

explanation.en: Dipole moment = charge × distance. F is most electronegative but the C–F bond is very short, so CH₃Cl (1.860 D) edges out CH₃F (1.847 D); then CH₃Br (1.830 D) and CH₃I (1.636 D).

stem.en: How many structural (constitutional) isomers are possible for C₄H₉Br?

explanation.en: 1-Bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane: four. (2-Bromobutane also has two enantiomers, but those are stereoisomers.)

stem.en: Which reagent converts ethanol to chloroethane with both by-products escaping as gases?

explanation.en: C₂H₅OH + SOCl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + SO₂↑ + HCl↑. Both by-products are gases, so pure chloroethane is left behind.

stem.en: The reaction CH₃CH₂Br + NaI → CH₃CH₂I + NaBr in dry acetone is called the:

explanation.en: Finkelstein reaction: halogen exchange with NaI in dry acetone. NaBr does not dissolve in acetone and precipitates, driving the reaction forward.

stem.en: Which has the highest boiling point?

explanation.en: For the same alkyl group, boiling point rises with molar mass and van der Waals forces: RI > RBr > RCl > RF.

stem.en: Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide to give mainly:

explanation.en: Peroxide effect (Kharasch): HBr adds by a free-radical path against Markovnikov’s rule, so Br goes to the terminal carbon: 1-bromopropane.

stem.en: Among the dichlorobenzenes, the highest melting point is shown by:

explanation.en: The para isomer is symmetrical and packs best in the crystal lattice, so it melts highest (about 323 K, against 256 K for ortho and 249 K for meta).

stem.en: Which alkyl bromide reacts fastest by the SN2 mechanism?

explanation.en: SN2 needs backside attack; bulky groups block it. Reactivity: CH₃X > 1° > 2° > 3°.

stem.en: The rate of an SN1 reaction depends on:

options.en: The concentration of the nucleophile only
The concentration of the alkyl halide only

explanation.en: In SN1 the slow step is ionisation of R–X into a carbocation; the nucleophile joins later in a fast step. Rate = k[R–X].

stem.en: An alkyl halide reacts with AgCN to give mainly:

explanation.en: AgCN is mainly covalent, so the Ag–C bond is not free; the nitrogen lone pair attacks, giving R–NC (isocyanide). Ionic KCN attacks through carbon, giving R–CN.

stem.en: Which of the following undergoes SN1 reaction fastest?

explanation.en: SN1 speed follows carbocation stability. (C₆H₅)₂CH⁺ is stabilised by resonance with two benzene rings, more than C₆H₅CH₂⁺ with one; primary and methyl cations are very unstable.

stem.en: For an SN2 reaction, rate = k[RX][OH⁻]. If [RX] is halved and [OH⁻] is doubled, the rate:

explanation.en: New rate = k(½[RX])(2[OH⁻]) = k[RX][OH⁻]: unchanged.

stem.en: A racemic mixture is optically inactive because of:

options.en: A plane of symmetry in each molecule

explanation.en: A racemic mixture has equal amounts of the d and l enantiomers; their opposite rotations cancel. This is external compensation. Internal compensation is the meso case.

stem.en: The major product when 2-bromobutane is heated with alcoholic KOH is:

explanation.en: Alcoholic KOH causes β-elimination. By Zaitsev’s rule the more substituted alkene, but-2-ene, is the major product (about 80%).

stem.en: Which of these molecules is chiral?

explanation.en: In 2-bromobutane C-2 carries four different groups: H, Br, CH₃ and C₂H₅. In the others, at least two groups on each carbon are identical.

stem.en: A mixture of CH₃Br and C₂H₅Br is treated with sodium in dry ether. The product is:

options.en: A mixture of ethane, propane and butane

explanation.en: Wurtz coupling joins any two alkyl groups at random: CH₃–CH₃ (ethane), CH₃–C₂H₅ (propane) and C₂H₅–C₂H₅ (butane). This is why Wurtz is used with one halide only.

stem.en: Grignard reagents must be prepared in dry ether because with water they:

explanation.en: R–MgX is a very strong base: R–MgX + H₂O → R–H + Mg(OH)X. Even traces of moisture destroy it, giving the alkane.

stem.en: Chlorobenzene is converted to phenol by heating with aqueous NaOH at:

explanation.en: Aryl halides resist nucleophilic substitution, so chlorobenzene needs NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification, to give phenol.

stem.en: Haloarenes are less reactive than haloalkanes towards nucleophilic substitution mainly because:

options.en: The C–X bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance
Halogens are less electronegative in arenes

explanation.en: The halogen lone pair is delocalised into the ring, giving the C–X bond partial double-bond character. The sp² carbon also makes the bond shorter and stronger, and the phenyl cation is unstable.

stem.en: C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na (dry ether) gives:

explanation.en: Wurtz–Fittig reaction joins an aryl and an alkyl group: C₆H₅–CH₃, toluene.

stem.en: Which compound undergoes nucleophilic substitution by OH⁻ most easily?

explanation.en: Nitro groups at ortho and para positions withdraw electrons and stabilise the carbanion intermediate. With three of them, 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene is hydrolysed by warm water.

stem.en: Chlorobenzene reacts with Cl₂ in the presence of anhydrous FeCl₃. The major product is:

explanation.en: Cl is an ortho/para director (lone-pair resonance), though deactivating. Para is less crowded, so 1,4-dichlorobenzene is the major product.
